title: The Products of Animal Origin (Disease Control) (Wales) (Amendment) Order 2026 / Gorchymyn Cynhyrchion sy’n Dod o Anifeiliaid (Rheoli Clefydau) (Cymru) (Diwygio) 2026
summary:
This Order amends the Products of Animal Origin (Disease Control) (Wales) Regulations 2008 (S.I. 2008/1275 (W. 132)) (“the 2008 Regulations”). The definitions of “disease” and “restricted meat” in the 2008 Regulations are updated, and a new Schedule 2 is substituted into the 2008 Regulations to reflect the current approved risk mitigating treatments for meat and casings.

title: The Air Departure Tax (Scotland) Amendment Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Air Departure Tax (Scotland) Act 2017 (“the 2017 Act”) to make provision concerning who is a non-chargeable passenger in respect of certain flights which begin or end at an airport in a designated area of Scotland and related consequential amendments to the 2017 Act. In addition, these Regulations amend section 9 of the 2017 Act (aircraft used under public service obligation).

The Air Departure Tax (Administration) (Scotland) Amendment Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the provisions concerning the administration of Air Departure Tax (“ADT”) in Part 4 (Payment, collection and management of tax) of the Air Departure Tax (Scotland) Act 2017 (“the 2017 Act”). In addition, these Regulations make amendments to section 44 (interpretation) and schedules 2 (minor and consequential modifications to Revenue Scotland and Tax Powers Act 2014) and 3 (index of defined expressions) of the 2017 Act, which are consequential upon the amendments made to Part 4.

title: The Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 (Commencement No. 1) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are the fourth set of commencement regulations bringing into force provisions of the Children’s Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 (c. 21) (“the Act”). They are the first set of regulations commencing provisions of the Act which substantively relate to a territory other than England, namely section 10 which relates to social care in England and Wales.

title: Correction Slip
summary: This Order amends the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (S.I. 2015/596) (“the GPDO”). The GPDO provides, for the purposes of section 59 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (c. 8), for the grant of planning permission for certain classes of development without the requirement for a planning application to be made under Part 3 of that Act. The classes of permission, known as “permitted development rights” together with their accompanying conditions, limitations and restrictions, are set out in Schedule 2 to the GPDO.

title: The Renewables Obligation and Electricity Capacity (Amendment) (British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme Excluded Electricity) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are made in exercise of the powers in sections 32, 32A, 32J and 32K of the Electricity Act 1989 (c. 29) and sections 27, 28, 30, 32, 33 and 40 of the Energy Act 2013 (c. 32). They make provision about BICS excluded electricity, which is a proportion of electricity measured by meters in respect of a manufacturing site which is used to carry out certain manufacturing activities (defined as “specified activity” in these Regulations). BICS excluded electricity is then excluded from the calculations of a supplier’s liability under the Renewables Obligation Order 2015 (S.I. 2015/1947), the Electricity Capacity (Supplier Payment etc.) Regulations 2014 (S.I. 2014/3354) and the Electricity Capacity (Supplier Payment etc.) (Amendment and Excluded Electricity) Regulations 2024 (S.I. 2024/434).

title: Administrative and Financial Provisions Act (Northern Ireland) 2026
summary: An Act to make further provision with respect to the administration and financing of public services in Northern Ireland, in particular, measures to provide powers to undertake certain activities, to enable charging for certain activities and to modify arrangements for financial governance.

title: Correction slip
summary: These Regulations, made under sections 51(3), 52(1) and 52(3) of the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006, specify fees relating to immigration and nationality. They follow on from the Immigration and Nationality (Fees) Order 2011, which sets out the applications, services and processes related to immigration and nationality in respect of which fees may be specified in regulations.
